title: Tokens and how to choose them
instruction: Choose a token step by step from its surface, and call it by name.
intro: Every color, size, space and speed in this guide comes from a design token: a named value kept in the token files, which the guide, the asset package and every product read. This chapter shows how the names work, when a new token may join, and how to choose the right one in five steps, with four worked examples to copy.
The files are tokens.css, for a web page, and tokens.json, for design tools and build scripts. Both hold the same 504 tokens and the same version, and Rule 26.8 has both to download.

groups.title: What a token is
groups.line: A token names one value for one job, and its name says which.

groups.title: Choosing a token
groups.line: Five steps take you from the surface to the token, and four examples show each step.

groups.title: Using the files
groups.line: Start a page from tokens.css, follow the reader’s light or dark setting, look up any token and download the files.

rules.title: Read every value through a token named for its job.
rule: A token is a named design value, and its name says its job and the surface it sits on. tokens.css and tokens.json hold the same 504 tokens in 13 categories: color, font, type, space, size, layout, radius, border, opacity, motion, z-index, chart and component. A name runs from its category to its surface: oa.color.text.secondary.onNewsprint in tokens.json is --oa-color-text-secondary-on-newsprint in CSS. Each part of the name is a word you can look up, so a name tells you its job.

Tokens come in three tiers. A primitive holds a value, such as Deep Stone. A semantic token gives a primitive one job on one surface, such as disabled text on Newsprint. A component token gives one part of one component its value, such as the label of an unavailable button, and points to a semantic token. Build with semantic and component tokens. A primitive is there for them to point to.

text: A name that says the job lets a page change its surface or its theme with no new value: a surface class or the dark theme points each short name at the token for that ground. A primitive cannot follow, because it names a color and nothing else.
why.basis: Design Tokens Format Module 2025.10; design judgment

correct.caption: One value in its three tiers. The button’s label reads the component token, which points to disabled text on Newsprint, which points to Deep Stone.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 26.1. The label reads the primitive itself. On Newsprint it passes; in the dark theme it stays Deep Stone on Charcoal and measures 2.42 to 1.

specs.label: Categories
specs.value: Color, font, type, space, size, layout, radius, border, opacity, motion, z-index, chart and component

specs.label: JSON name
specs.value: Segments in camel case, the surface last: oa.color.text.secondary.onNewsprint

specs.label: CSS name
specs.value: --oa-, then the segments in kebab case: --oa-color-text-secondary-on-newsprint

specs.label: Short name
specs.value: The CSS name without its surface, --oa-color-text-secondary, set by a surface class or a theme (Rule 26.6)

specs.label: Tiers
specs.value: Primitive, semantic, component. A token points only to a tier below it

builders: Search the table in Rule 26.7 by any word of a name. Its tier is in the fourth column.

rules.title: Add a token only when it meets all five conditions.
rule: A new token joins tokens.json only when it meets five conditions, and the plates below check two values against them. The need comes first: one that no token meets, registered with an ID and its evidence. The value must be one palette color mixed in OKLab toward Newsprint or Charcoal, with the amount recorded. A token does one job, said in one sentence, and its contrast passes on every surface it serves at the threshold its kind needs, with the ratio stored. Last, its record holds a description, a tier and a status.

Look in the table first (Rule 26.7). Most needs already have a token, and a second token for one job leaves builders to guess between them. Values that failed stay on record as held or rejected, and nothing uses them.

text: Each token is a value someone must test, describe and keep. The five conditions keep the set small and every token’s reason on record, so the next person who asks why a gray exists can read the answer in the file.

correct.caption: Deep Stone meets all five. Stone measured 4.29 to 1 for small secondary text, and Deep Stone answers that need with one job.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 26.2. A second red for marks passes its contrast at 3.22 to 1, and still fails three conditions: no need, no recorded mix and a job already taken.

specs.label: Value
specs.value: One palette color mixed in OKLab toward Newsprint or Charcoal, in CSS through color-mix(in oklab, …)

specs.label: Contrast
specs.value: 4.5 to 1 for text, 3 to 1 for large text, needed graphics and focus rings, on every surface the token serves

specs.label: Record
specs.value: $description, tier and status in the token’s own entry; the need’s ID and evidence in the file’s register

specs.label: Release
specs.value: A new token raises the version’s second number (Rule 26.8)

builders: Ask the editor for a token before you add a value of your own. Send the need and its evidence with the request, and the five conditions decide.

rules.title: Choose a token in five steps, starting from its surface.
rule: The five steps are surface, role, emphasis, state, then any component token, which wins. Start from the surface the element sits on: Newsprint, White, Charcoal or Prussian. Then its job, which a token’s name calls its role: text, graphic, border, focus, data, action, state or field. Then its emphasis: primary or secondary text, an essential or subtle graphic, a strong or hairline border, the data a chart is about or its context. Then its state, if it has one, such as selected, disabled, warning or error. Last, look for a component token for the part you are drawing, such as a button’s disabled label. When one exists, use it, since it already holds the component’s own choice.

A message with no state of its own, such as a correction notice, takes primary text for its words and the essential graphic for its 4 px bar: --oa-color-text-primary, and --oa-color-graphic-essential at --oa-border-width-bar. Leave the strong border to the edges of fields and controls, since a change to those edges would move the notice too.

In CSS the first step is the theme or a class. With tokens.css linked, the theme points every short name at the tokens for the page’s ground, Newsprint in the light theme and Charcoal in the dark one. A block that must keep one ground in both themes takes a surface class: .oa-surface-prussian points every short name inside it at Prussian’s tokens. Either way your code names the role alone, --oa-color-text-secondary, and draws right on whatever ground the block sits on.

text: Each step narrows the choice by a fact about the page, so two builders reach the same token. Every color token was measured on its own surface, and starting from the surface keeps you on the one it was measured for.

correct.caption: A caption on a Charcoal panel: surface Charcoal, role text, emphasis secondary, no state, no component token. The token is Dim Newsprint, 7.26 to 1.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 26.3. The first step was skipped, and a caption on Prussian took Newsprint’s secondary text token: 1.72 to 1.

specs.label: 1 Surface
specs.value: Newsprint, White, Charcoal or Prussian; in CSS, .oa-surface-newsprint and the rest, or the theme (Rule 26.6)

specs.label: 2 Role
specs.value: The token’s job: text, graphic, border, focus, data, action, state, field

specs.label: 3 Emphasis
specs.value: Primary or secondary text; essential or subtle graphic; strong or hairline border; emphasis or context in data

specs.label: 4 State
specs.value: Muted, disabled, loading, selected, warning, error, empty, success; hover and focus have their own tokens (chapter 17)

specs.label: 5 Component
specs.value: A token under oa.component for the part you draw; it wins over the token the first four steps reach

specs.label: No state
specs.value: A notice with no state: --oa-color-text-primary words, a --oa-color-graphic-essential bar at --oa-border-width-bar

builders: Write the role’s short name in your CSS. Add a surface class in your HTML only where a block must keep one ground in both themes, such as a Prussian panel. A component then needs no change to move from one surface or theme to another.

rules.title: Work through the five steps on four common parts.
rule: The four examples below take parts every product needs through the five steps of Rule 26.3, and set each at actual size beside its failure, with code to copy. Each code set reads only tokens.css, by short name, with a surface class where the example names a surface. Its live demos show it in the light theme and the dark theme, so you can see each token follow the ground.

text: A worked example shows the choice at each step and the ratio it buys, so you can check a new part the same way before you ship it.

examples.title: A caption under a chart, on Newsprint

correct.caption: Surface Newsprint, role text, emphasis secondary: Deep Stone, 5.49 to 1.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 26.4. Stone looks close, and it is a graphic’s color: 4.29 to 1, under the 4.5 to 1 small text needs.

code.name: Chart caption
code.caption: The caption reads --oa-color-text-secondary, so it is Deep Stone on Newsprint and Dim Newsprint on Charcoal.

examples.title: A download button that waits for a choice, on White

correct.caption: Surface White, role action, state disabled, then the button’s own tokens, which win: a dashed edge and a label at 7.74 to 1, with the reason under it.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 26.4. The button is faded to 40 percent: 2.61 to 1, and nothing says why it waits.

code.name: Download button that waits
code.caption: The block carries .oa-surface-white, so the button draws on White in both themes. It keeps focus and points to its reason.

examples.title: A highlighted bar in a chart, on Newsprint

correct.caption: Surface Newsprint, role data: emphasis for the bar the headline names, context for the rest. Charcoal 13.29 to 1, Stone 4.29 to 1, 3.10 to 1 apart.

failure.caption: Fails Rules 26.4 and 05.3. The highlight takes Pillar Red with no keyline, 2.96 to 1, while an error already holds the view’s red.

code.name: Bar chart with one bar highlighted
code.caption: The bars read --oa-color-data-emphasis and --oa-color-data-context, and every bar carries its count.

examples.title: A warning in a tracker, on Prussian

correct.caption: Surface Prussian, role state, state warning: the words in White, 13.28 to 1, the bar and triangle in Newsprint, 9.42 to 1, and the word Warning.

failure.caption: Fails Rules 26.4 and 05.3. Red words on Prussian, 3.19 to 1, with no word and no mark.

code.name: Warning in a tracker
code.caption: The block carries .oa-surface-prussian, so the warning reads Prussian’s tokens in both themes.

specs.label: Caption
specs.value: --oa-color-text-secondary, caption type: 5.49 to 1 on Newsprint, 7.26 on Charcoal

specs.label: Button that waits
specs.value: --oa-component-button-disabled-label and -edge, dashed: 7.74 to 1 on White, with a reason line

specs.label: Highlighted bar
specs.value: --oa-color-data-emphasis beside --oa-color-data-context: 13.29 and 4.29 to 1 on Newsprint, 3.10 apart

specs.label: Warning on Prussian
specs.value: --oa-color-state-warning-text and -mark: 13.28 and 9.42 to 1, with the triangle and the word

builders: Each code set’s CSS opens with the five steps it took and the ratios they give, so you can follow the same path for a part of your own.

rules.title: Start every page from tokens.css: link it, then set the body’s margin and type.
rule: Link the brand’s fonts and tokens.css before your own styles, then give the body one rule: body { margin: 0; font: var(--oa-type-body) }. It sets Inter at 17 px with a line height of 1.6 wherever text asks for no other style, and removes the browser’s 8 px margin, so a component sits where its code puts it. Leave the body with no surface class, so the theme sets its ground (Rule 26.6).

A product that follows the reader’s light or dark setting also declares <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark"> in its head, so the browser draws its own scroll bars and form controls to match. If it offers the theme switch of Rule 18.4, the head script comes first, before the stylesheets, so a stored choice applies before the page first draws (Rule 26.6).

tokens.css holds tokens and themes and nothing else. A page that draws one of the 41 symbols at 24 px (Rules 09.3 and 10.4) also needs the two lines that show the pixel fit on a screen under 2x and the master from 2x: .oa-at-2x { display: none } and @media (min-resolution: 2dppx) { .oa-at-1x { display: none } .oa-at-2x { display: inline } }.

text: Every code set in chapters 18 and 26 assumes exactly this page. The guide checks each one by pasting its code into a page that holds the fonts, tokens.css and this body rule and nothing else, then compares what it draws, and the styles each part computes, with the live demo. Rule 19.8’s results list any difference.

correct.caption: The head of a page started from tokens.css, and the body text it draws against the window’s edge, with no margin.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 26.5. With the body rule left out, the text falls back to the browser’s serif at 16 px inside an 8 px margin.

specs.label: Order in the head
specs.value: For a product with the theme switch, the head script first (Rule 26.6); then the color scheme meta tag, the fonts, tokens.css and your own styles

specs.label: Body rule
specs.value: body { margin: 0; font: var(--oa-type-body) }

specs.label: Fonts
specs.value: Inter 400, 600 and 700, Inter Tight 800 and Lora Italic 400 and 500, from Google Fonts under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (Rule 06.10). This guide carries the same files inside the page.

specs.label: Themed product
specs.value: <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">; a page that stays light writes only light

specs.label: 24 px symbols
specs.value: .oa-at-2x { display: none } and @media (min-resolution: 2dppx) { .oa-at-1x { display: none } .oa-at-2x { display: inline } }, in your own stylesheet

builders: A product loads the three faces with this link (Rule 06.10): https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;600;700&family=Inter+Tight:wght@800&family=Lora:ital,wght@1,400;1,500&display=swap. This guide carries the same files inside the page, unchanged, so it loads no type from elsewhere; its colophon holds their licenses.

rules.title: Let a product follow the reader’s light or dark setting through one attribute.
rule: tokens.css carries a light theme on Newsprint and a dark theme on Charcoal. With no attribute on the page’s root, a page follows the device. data-oa-theme="light" or "dark" on the root wins over the device, and "device" hands the choice back. On any other element the attribute sets that element and everything inside it.

A reader’s switch (Rule 18.4) stores Light or Dark under the key oa-theme, and Match my device removes it. A short script in the head applies a stored choice before the page first draws, so it never flashes the wrong ground. Paint a menu’s or dialog’s own ground with --oa-color-surface, and an entry box’s with --oa-color-field-ground, so both follow the theme.

A surface class keeps its own ground in both themes. In a product that follows the theme, put no surface class on the body, or on any block that should follow it. Use one only where a block must keep one ground, as the White and Prussian examples of Rule 26.4 do.

A few roles have no Charcoal token yet and stay unset in the dark theme: the diverging chart scale, the Error Band, and two keylines red needs only on Newsprint, the ask button’s and a chart point’s. An error on Charcoal keeps its bar, mark and words with no band.

text: One set of short names serves both grounds, so a component written once draws correctly in both themes, as each code plate in chapter 18 shows live. A token named for one surface cannot follow.
why.basis: Media Queries Level 5, prefers-color-scheme; design judgment

correct.caption: One card, two themes, the same short names. Secondary text measures 5.49 to 1 on Newsprint and 7.26 on Charcoal.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 26.6. The words name Newsprint’s text token, so in the dark theme they stay Charcoal on Charcoal: 1.00 to 1.

specs.label: Attribute
specs.value: data-oa-theme: light, dark or device; none follows the device

specs.label: Storage
specs.value: oa-theme in localStorage, holding light or dark; Match my device removes it

specs.label: Head script
specs.value: try { var t = localStorage.getItem('oa-theme'); if (t === 'light' || t === 'dark') document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-oa-theme', t); } catch (e) {}

specs.label: Grounds
specs.value: --oa-color-surface for a menu or dialog; --oa-color-field-ground for an entry box

specs.label: Unset in the dark theme
specs.value: The diverging chart scale, the Error Band, the ask button’s keyline and a chart point’s keyline

builders: Leave the body with no surface class, so the theme sets its ground. Put the head script in its own script element before the stylesheets. Rule 18.4 has the switch and its script to copy.

rules.title: Look up any token in the table, and copy its name from there.
rule: The table lists every token in tokens.json, 504 in all, in 17 groups, each closed until you open it. The groups follow Rule 26.1’s 13 categories, with color split into four groups and chart into two, font listed as “Type: faces and weights” and z-index as “Stacking order”. A row gives the token’s name in the JSON and in CSS, its value, its job, its tier and, for a color, the contrast it measures on each surface it serves. Search by any of those words, and every group that holds a match opens. Copy puts the CSS name on your clipboard.

text: A name copied from the source cannot drift, and a value typed by hand stays as it was when the next release changes the token.

correct.caption: Every token in tokens.json, version 6.0.0-gate2.9. Search, then copy a name.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 26.7. A gray typed from an old file, #4E535C, where Deep Stone’s name belongs. It matches today and falls behind with the next release.

specs.label: Rows
specs.value: 504, in 17 groups by category, each closed until opened; the list above them opens one

specs.label: Search
specs.value: Any word of a name, a value, a job or a tier; every group with a match opens, and the line beside the field says how many rows show

specs.label: Copy
specs.value: The CSS name, with a line that says what was copied, or what to do when the browser refuses

builders: The Use column prints each token’s description from tokens.json word for word, and a deprecated token says which name replaced it.

rules.title: Read the version before you update, and download both token files here.
rule: tokens.css and tokens.json carry one version number, in three parts. A renamed or removed token, or a changed palette color, raises the first part, and may break a page. A new token, or a changed value that still passes its contrast, raises the second. A change to descriptions alone raises the third.

A replaced token keeps its old CSS name as an alias for one more release of the second part, marked as deprecated, so a page that reads it keeps working while you move it. Every version comes with a change note: its date, the tokens it touches, what changed and why.

The files in this draft carry 6.0.0-gate2.9. The part after the hyphen marks a draft before 6.0.0, the first release. Since 6.0.0-gate2.8, --oa-color-state-error-mark is the deprecated old name of --oa-color-state-error-bar, and it leaves with 6.1.0.

text: A builder who reads the first part of the number knows at once whether an update can break a page, and the note says what to change.

correct.caption: The change note for 6.0.0-gate2.9, as tokens.json records it.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 26.8. A token renamed in a release of the second part, with no alias and no note. A page’s caption loses its gray, and nothing warns.

specs.label: First part
specs.value: A renamed or removed token, or a changed palette color

specs.label: Second part
specs.value: A new token, or a changed value that still passes its contrast

specs.label: Third part
specs.value: Descriptions and notes alone

specs.label: Deprecated token
specs.value: Its old CSS name stays as an alias for one more release of the second part

specs.label: Files
specs.value: tokens.css for a web page; tokens.json, in the Design Tokens Format Module 2025.10, for design tools and build scripts

builders: Read the change note before you update a product’s copy of tokens.css. The newest note also sits at the top of the file.
